title: Guoding Liu · Quantum Information
background: Quantum-information theory using random circuits, representation theory, stabilizer formalism and decoupling. Research connects device benchmarking and certification with QEC and resource-dependent quantum advantages.
research_questions: Can a fixed noisy multi-qubit gate be certified using trusted local controls, without a trusted inverse or short-time Hamiltonian access, robust to small non-repeatable SPAM? What are the shot, sequence length and target-call costs?
Which bounded-error logical primitives and syndrome or logical-output data identify logical fidelity for a fixed code, recovery and gadget? What physical-noise and memory assumptions are necessary?
Which tasks have nearly optimal depth, ancilla and magic costs simultaneously? What tradeoffs or lower bounds arise under locality and adaptive measurement?
How do design order, scrambling and decoupling affect encoding, noisy-state discrimination and single-copy learning?
Which quantum-data tasks reveal an operational advantage from magic, measurement access, coherent processing or timing of classical side information?
Can high-order fermionic designs reduce total single-copy sample complexity, beyond improved tails or additional quantum memory?
exclusions: Generic variational quantum machine learning on classical datasets without rigorous quantum-data guarantees
Quantum chemistry calculations without a connection to measurement, shadows or fermionic information theory
Hardware materials and spectroscopy without a concrete characterization or error-correction connection
Purely software engineering or heuristic benchmarking of classical simulators
